output.title: Dormant clients are a follow-up workflow problem
output.body:
Dormant clients are not a vague business mood. They are a follow-up and reactivation workflow problem: a list that stops moving, while someone still has to decide who to contact, when, and with what message.

For a small business, the quiet cost usually shows up in manual checks and half-finished re-engagement. The owner or a helper looks at old contacts, wonders which ones are worth another try, and then spends time sorting by memory instead of by a rule. That is the part worth fixing first.

The bounded decision is simple: do you keep dormant-client review manual, or do you set up a small workflow that flags contacts by last-contact date and segments them for review? If the pattern is frequent and repeatable, that is a reasonable place to consider automation. If the list is tiny or changes rarely, manual review may be enough.

The next step is practical: export the dormant-client list, add a last-contact date, and review the oldest contacts first. That gives you a clear threshold for whether the work is just annoying, or whether it is becoming a recurring process problem. Human approval still stays with the owner before any outreach is sent. Sometimes the spreadsheet is the real bottleneck, not the client.
